name: Diabetes
description: A chronic metabolic disease characterized by elevated blood glucose levels leading to vascular and organ complications.
causes: Insulin resistance or insufficient insulin production by pancreatic beta cells.
generalGuidance: Blood glucose monitoring, dietary management, insulin therapy under physician guidance.
redFlags: Severe lethargy with fruity acetone breath odor
whenToSeekCare: Seek immediate care for severe confusion, rapid breathing, or blood glucose > 300 mg/dL.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by glycemic and hormonal biomarker laboratory panels.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Hypertension
description: Long-term high blood pressure against arterial walls causing increased cardiac workload.
causes: Arterial stiffening, genetic factors, excessive sodium intake, renal dysfunction.
generalGuidance: Periodic blood pressure tracking, DASH diet, anti-hypertensive medications.
redFlags: Crushing chest pressure radiating to arm or jaw
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent care for blood pressure > 180/120 mm Hg or sudden severe headache/chest pain.
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by exertional triggers and cardiac biomarker changes.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Heart Disease
description: Range of cardiac conditions including coronary artery disease and heart muscle dysfunction.
causes: Atherosclerotic plaque accumulation narrowing coronary arteries.
generalGuidance: Cardiac rehabilitation, lipid-lowering medication, lifestyle modification.
redFlags: Crushing chest pressure radiating to arm or jaw
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care immediately for crushing chest pain, arm radiation, or severe shortness of breath.
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by exertional triggers and cardiac biomarker changes.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Asthma
description: Chronic inflammatory disease of airway passages causing episodic wheezing and bronchospasm.
causes: Environmental allergens, airway hyper-responsiveness, respiratory viral infections.
generalGuidance: Inhaled corticosteroids, quick-relief bronchodilators, asthma action plan.
redFlags: Severe shortness of breath at rest
Inability to speak in full sentences
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care for severe chest tightness, inability to speak full sentences, or blue lips.
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by respiratory auscultation findings and sputum characteristics.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Pneumonia
description: Inflammatory infection of pulmonary alveoli filled with fluid or purulent exudate.
causes: Bacterial (Streptococcus pneumoniae), viral (Influenza, RSV), or fungal pathogens.
generalGuidance: Targeted antibiotic or antiviral therapy, adequate hydration, fever management.
redFlags: Severe shortness of breath at rest
Inability to speak in full sentences
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent medical attention for high fever, chest pain during breathing, or severe oxygen drop.
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by respiratory auscultation findings and sputum characteristics.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Tuberculosis
description: Contagious bacterial infection affecting pulmonary tissue caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
causes: Inhalation of airborne droplet nuclei containing M. tuberculosis.
riskFactors: close contact with active TB cases
generalGuidance: Strict 6-month anti-tubercular drug regimen (DOTS protocol).
redFlags: Severe shortness of breath at rest
Inability to speak in full sentences
whenToSeekCare: Seek immediate evaluation for coughing up blood, persistent night sweats, or unexplained weight loss.
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by respiratory auscultation findings and sputum characteristics.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: COVID-19
description: Acute infectious disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus variant.
causes: Respiratory transmission of SARS-CoV-2 viral particles.
generalGuidance: Symptomatic control, hydration, antiviral drugs for high-risk patients.
redFlags: Severe shortness of breath at rest
Inability to speak in full sentences
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care for persistent chest pressure, oxygen saturation < 94%, or confusion.
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by respiratory auscultation findings and sputum characteristics.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Influenza
description: Acute viral infection of upper and lower respiratory tracts caused by influenza viruses.
causes: Infection by Influenza A or B viral strains.
prevention: avoiding close contact with sick persons.
generalGuidance: Rest, fluid intake, antiviral treatment (Oseltamivir) within 48 hours of onset.
redFlags: Severe shortness of breath at rest
Inability to speak in full sentences
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical attention if fever persists over 4 days or severe breathing difficulty develops.
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by respiratory auscultation findings and sputum characteristics.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Dengue
description: Mosquito-borne viral infection causing severe flu-like illness and low blood platelets.
causes: Transmission of Dengue virus (DENV-1-4) by infected Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.
generalGuidance: Supportive care, continuous hydration, monitoring blood platelet count.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care for severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, or mucosal bleeding.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Malaria
description: Life-threatening parasitic infection transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes.
causes: Plasmodium parasite infection (P. falciparum, P. vivax).
generalGuidance: Artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACT) prescribed by physicians.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Seek immediate medical attention for high cyclical fever, severe chills, or jaundice.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Typhoid
description: Systemic bacterial fever caused by Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi.
causes: Ingestion of food or water contaminated with S. Typhi bacteria.
generalGuidance: Targeted oral/intravenous antibiotics and fever control.
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical care for continuous high fever, Rose spots on abdomen, or severe lethargy.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by relation to meals, stool characteristics, and localized peritoneal signs.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Migraine
description: Recurrent neurological headache disorder characterized by moderate-to-severe throbbing pain.
causes: Neurovascular reactivity, trigeminal nerve activation, serotonin level fluctuations.
generalGuidance: Acute triptan therapy, preventive medications, dark room rest.
redFlags: Focal neurological deficits (facial droop, arm weakness)
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent evaluation for a sudden "thunderclap" headache or accompanied facial numbness/weakness.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by neurological exam and temporal symptom onset.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Epilepsy
description: Central nervous system disorder characterized by recurrent unprovoked electrical seizures.
causes: Abnormal brain electrical activity due to genetics, head trauma, stroke, or structural brain lesions.
generalGuidance: Antiepileptic drugs (AEDs), regular neurological monitoring.
redFlags: Focal neurological deficits (facial droop, arm weakness)
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency services if a seizure lasts longer than 5 minutes or consecutive seizures occur.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by neurological exam and temporal symptom onset.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Parkinson's Disease
description: Progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by loss of dopamine-producing brain cells.
causes: Degeneration of substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons, alpha-synuclein accumulation.
generalGuidance: Levodopa/Carbidopa medication, physical therapy, occupational assistance.
redFlags: Focal neurological deficits (facial droop, arm weakness)
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical advice upon noticing resting hand tremors, muscle rigidity, or gait disturbance.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by neurological exam and temporal symptom onset.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Alzheimer's Disease
description: Progressive neurodegenerative disease causing memory impairment and cognitive decline.
causes: Accumulation of extracellular amyloid-beta plaques and intracellular tau tangles.
generalGuidance: Cholinesterase inhibitors, supportive cognitive care, safety modifications.
redFlags: Focal neurological deficits (facial droop, arm weakness)
whenToSeekCare: Seek neurological assessment for progressive short-term memory loss interfering with daily living.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by neurological exam and temporal symptom onset.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: COPD
description: Progressive airflow limitation caused by emphysema and chronic bronchitis.
causes: Long-term exposure to irritating gases, primarily cigarette smoke or biomass fuel.
generalGuidance: Inhaled bronchodilators, pulmonary rehabilitation, supplemental oxygen therapy.
redFlags: Severe shortness of breath at rest
Inability to speak in full sentences
whenToSeekCare: Seek immediate emergency care for acute exacerbation with severe breathlessness and cyanosis.
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by respiratory auscultation findings and sputum characteristics.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Bronchitis
description: Inflammation of bronchial mucosal lining leading to productive cough.
causes: Viral respiratory infections (rhinovirus, influenza) or acute chemical irritants.
generalGuidance: Expectorants, hydration, rest, avoiding respiratory irritants.
redFlags: Severe shortness of breath at rest
Inability to speak in full sentences
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical consultation if cough persists over 3 weeks or sputum contains blood.
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by respiratory auscultation findings and sputum characteristics.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Gastritis
description: Inflammation or erosion of the protective gastric mucosal lining.
causes: Helicobacter pylori bacterial infection, chronic NSAID use, excessive alcohol.
prevention: avoid excessive alcohol and spicy trigger foods.
generalGuidance: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), antacids, H. pylori antibiotic eradication.
whenToSeekCare: Seek immediate medical care for vomiting blood, dark tarry stools, or severe stomach pain.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by relation to meals, stool characteristics, and localized peritoneal signs.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Hepatitis
description: Inflammation of liver tissue caused primarily by viral pathogens or toxins.
causes: Hepatitis viruses (A, B, C, D, E), heavy alcohol consumption, autoimmune reactions.
generalGuidance: Antiviral medications, supportive liver care, complete alcohol abstinence.
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent medical attention for yellowing skin/eyes (jaundice) or dark brown urine.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by relation to meals, stool characteristics, and localized peritoneal signs.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Fatty Liver Disease
description: Excessive accumulation of triglycerides within hepatic cells (steatosis).
causes: Metabolic dysfunction, insulin resistance, high fructose intake, heavy alcohol consumption.
generalGuidance: Dietary modification, lifestyle intervention, managing blood glucose.
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation if experiencing persistent right upper quadrant abdominal discomfort.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by relation to meals, stool characteristics, and localized peritoneal signs.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Chronic Kidney Disease
description: Gradual loss of renal filtration function over months to years.
causes: Uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, long-standing hypertension, glomerulonephritis.
prevention: Strict blood sugar and blood pressure control
generalGuidance: Renoprotective medications (ACE inhibitors), renal diet, dialysis in advanced stages.
redFlags: High fever with severe flank rigors
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for swelling in legs/ankles, decreased urine output, or persistent nausea.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by urinalysis and renal function indices.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Urinary Tract Infection (UTI)
description: Infection of urinary structures, most commonly the urinary bladder (cystitis).
causes: Bacterial colonization (Escherichia coli) ascending through urethra into urinary bladder.
generalGuidance: Targeted antibiotic therapy, increased water intake.
redFlags: High fever with severe flank rigors
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent medical attention if experiencing high fever, flank/back pain, or severe chills.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by urinalysis and renal function indices.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Anemia
description: Deficiency in healthy red blood cells or hemoglobin concentration impaired oxygen delivery.
causes: Iron deficiency, vitamin B12/folate deficiency, chronic blood loss, bone marrow failure.
generalGuidance: Iron/vitamin supplementation, addressing underlying blood loss cause.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Seek immediate care for severe shortness of breath, dizziness upon standing, or chest tightness.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Hypothyroidism
description: Underactive thyroid gland producing insufficient thyroid hormones (T3/T4).
causes: Hashimoto autoimmune thyroiditis, thyroidectomy, iodine deficiency.
generalGuidance: Daily levothyroxine hormone replacement therapy.
redFlags: Severe lethargy with fruity acetone breath odor
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical review for progressive unexplained weight gain, extreme fatigue, or cold intolerance.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by glycemic and hormonal biomarker laboratory panels.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Hyperthyroidism
description: Overactive thyroid gland producing excessive thyroid hormones.
causes: Graves autoimmune disease, toxic multinodular goiter, thyroiditis.
generalGuidance: Anti-thyroid medications (Methimazole), beta-blockers, radioactive iodine.
redFlags: Severe lethargy with fruity acetone breath odor
whenToSeekCare: Seek immediate medical attention for rapid irregular heart rate (palpitations) or severe tremors.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by glycemic and hormonal biomarker laboratory panels.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Common Cold
description: A mild viral infectious disease of the upper respiratory tract primarily affecting the nasal mucosa and throat.
causes: Rhinoviruses, coronaviruses, adenoviruses, or enteroviruses.
generalGuidance: Rest, oral hydration, warm saline gargles, over-the-counter decongestants or analgesics as appropriate.
redFlags: Severe shortness of breath at rest
Inability to speak in full sentences
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical care if symptoms persist beyond 10-14 days, high fever develops, or wheezing occurs.
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by respiratory auscultation findings and sputum characteristics.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Allergic Rhinitis
description: Inflammation of the interior nasal passages caused by an IgE-mediated allergic response to inhaled environmental allergens.
causes: Inhaled allergens including tree/grass pollen, house dust mites, animal dander, and fungal spores.
riskFactors: family history of asthma or eczema
prevention: keep windows closed during high pollen counts.
generalGuidance: Nasal corticosteroid sprays, oral second-generation antihistamines, saline nasal rinses, allergen immunotherapy.
redFlags: Severe shortness of breath at rest
Inability to speak in full sentences
whenToSeekCare: Seek evaluation if chronic nasal obstruction causes secondary sinusitis or impairs quality of sleep.
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by respiratory auscultation findings and sputum characteristics.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Sinusitis
description: Inflammation or infection of the mucosal lining of the paranasal sinuses, causing facial pressure and nasal congestion.
causes: Secondary bacterial infection following viral upper respiratory infection, allergic swelling, or anatomical nasal polyps.
prevention: Prompt management of colds and allergies
generalGuidance: Nasal saline irrigation, decongestants, intranasal steroids, oral antibiotics if bacterial infection confirmed.
redFlags: Severe shortness of breath at rest
Inability to speak in full sentences
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent medical care if experiencing severe headache, periorbital swelling, vision changes, or high fever.
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by respiratory auscultation findings and sputum characteristics.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Heart Failure
description: A chronic, progressive condition in which the cardiac muscle is unable to pump sufficient blood volume to meet systemic metabolic demands.
causes: Long-standing hypertension, prior myocardial infarction, coronary artery disease, cardiomyopathy, or valvular heart disease.
generalGuidance: ACE inhibitors/ARNs, beta-blockers, aldosterone antagonists, SGLT2 inhibitors, diuretics, fluid restriction, daily weight tracking.
redFlags: Crushing chest pressure radiating to arm or jaw
whenToSeekCare: Seek immediate emergency care for sudden severe breathlessness, inability to lie flat, or rapid unexplained weight gain (>3 lbs in 24h).
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by exertional triggers and cardiac biomarker changes.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Arrhythmia
description: Disruptions or irregularities in the electrical conduction system of the heart, resulting in bradycardia, tachycardia, or fibrillatory rhythm.
causes: Ischemic heart disease, electrolyte imbalances, structural cardiac remodeling, caffeine, thyroid disease, or electrical channelopathies.
generalGuidance: Anti-arrhythmic medications, rate-control agents (beta-blockers), catheter ablation, cardioversion, pacemakers or ICDs.
redFlags: Crushing chest pressure radiating to arm or jaw
whenToSeekCare: Seek immediate emergency medical care for palpitations accompanied by syncope, chest pain, or severe dizziness.
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by exertional triggers and cardiac biomarker changes.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Angina Pectoris
description: Reversible chest pain or pressure resulting from transient myocardial ischemia due to inadequate coronary blood flow.
causes: Atherosclerotic coronary artery stenosis restricting oxygen delivery during times of increased myocardial workload.
generalGuidance: Sublingual nitroglycerin for acute episodes, beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers, statins, antiplatelet therapy.
redFlags: Crushing chest pressure radiating to arm or jaw
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency medical services immediately if chest pain lasts longer than 10 minutes or does not resolve with rest and nitroglycerin.
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by exertional triggers and cardiac biomarker changes.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Peripheral Artery Disease
description: A circulatory condition in which atherosclerotic plaque narrows peripheral arteries, severely reducing blood flow to the limbs.
causes: Systemic atherosclerosis affecting the abdominal aorta, iliac, femoral, and popliteal arterial branches.
generalGuidance: Supervised exercise therapy, antiplatelet medications (aspirin/clopidogrel), statin therapy, cilostazol, endovascular revascularization.
redFlags: Crushing chest pressure radiating to arm or jaw
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent care for resting foot pain, cold/pale extremities, or non-healing ulcers on the lower extremities.
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by exertional triggers and cardiac biomarker changes.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Prediabetes
description: A metabolic state where blood glucose levels are above normal ranges (HbA1c 5.7-6.4%) but not yet meeting the threshold for type 2 diabetes.
causes: Progressive peripheral insulin resistance coupled with relative pancreatic beta-cell secretory compensation.
prevention: Structured lifestyle interventions: 7% sustained weight reduction
generalGuidance: Intensive dietary modification, aerobic and resistance training, routine HbA1c monitoring every 6-12 months, metformin where indicated.
redFlags: Severe lethargy with fruity acetone breath odor
whenToSeekCare: Consult a physician for routine screening if persistent fatigue, increased thirst, or unexplained weight shifts occur.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by glycemic and hormonal biomarker laboratory panels.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Obesity
description: A complex, chronic multifactorial disease characterized by excessive adiposity that impairs physical and metabolic health.
causes: Energy imbalance between caloric consumption and metabolic expenditure, neuroendocrine appetite regulation dysregulation, genetics.
generalGuidance: Comprehensive lifestyle therapy, medical nutritional therapy, pharmacotherapy (GLP-1 receptor agonists), bariatric metabolic surgery.
redFlags: Severe lethargy with fruity acetone breath odor
whenToSeekCare: Seek healthcare consultation when excess weight contributes to joint pain, obstructive sleep apnea, or metabolic dysregulation.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by glycemic and hormonal biomarker laboratory panels.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
description: A prevalent endocrine disorder in reproductive-aged females characterized by ovulatory dysfunction, hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovarian morphology.
causes: Complex genetic, neuroendocrine, and metabolic factors with underlying hyperinsulinemia and ovarian theca-cell androgen overproduction.
prevention: regular physical activity to enhance peripheral insulin sensitivity.
generalGuidance: Combined oral contraceptives, metformin for insulin resistance, lifestyle modification, anti-androgens (spironolactone), ovulation induction.
redFlags: Severe lethargy with fruity acetone breath odor
whenToSeekCare: Consult a gynecologist or endocrinologist for irregular menstrual cycles, severe cystic acne, or difficulty conceiving.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by glycemic and hormonal biomarker laboratory panels.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: GERD (Acid Reflux)
description: A chronic gastrointestinal disorder where stomach acid persistently refluxes backward into the esophagus, irritating the mucosal lining.
causes: Transient lower esophageal sphincter (LES) relaxations, hiatal hernia, delayed gastric emptying, increased intra-abdominal pressure.
prevention: avoid recumbency within 3 hours of meals
generalGuidance: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), H2-receptor antagonists, antacids, lifestyle modifications, endoscopic or surgical fundoplication.
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt evaluation for progressive dysphagia (trouble swallowing), unintentional weight loss, hematemesis, or anemia.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by relation to meals, stool characteristics, and localized peritoneal signs.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
description: Erosive mucosal lesions occurring in the protective inner lining of the stomach (gastric ulcer) or proximal small intestine (duodenal ulcer).
causes: Helicobacter pylori bacterial colonization, chronic usage of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), hyperacidity.
prevention: co-prescribe gastroprotection (PPIs) when chronic NSAIDs are required
generalGuidance: Antibiotic eradication therapy for H. pylori, proton pump inhibitors, mucosal protective agents, avoiding mucosal irritants.
whenToSeekCare: Seek immediate emergency evaluation for vomiting frank blood or coffee-ground emesis, black tarry stools, or sudden acute abdominal pain.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by relation to meals, stool characteristics, and localized peritoneal signs.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Gastroenteritis
description: An acute inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract mucous membranes, involving both stomach and small intestine.
causes: Viral pathogens (Norovirus, Rotavirus), bacterial toxins (Salmonella, Campylobacter, E. coli), or parasitic protozoa.
riskFactors: Consumption of contaminated water or unpasteurized food
prevention: Meticulous hand washing with soap and water
generalGuidance: Oral rehydration therapy with balanced electrolyte solutions, gradual reintroduction of bland diet, zinc supplementation, antiemetics if needed.
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent care if signs of dehydration emerge (sunken eyes, dizziness, absence of urination), bloody stool, or inability to tolerate liquids.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by relation to meals, stool characteristics, and localized peritoneal signs.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)
description: A common disorder of the brain-gut interaction characterized by recurrent abdominal pain related to defecation or changes in bowel habits.
causes: Visceral hypersensitivity, altered gut-brain communication, gastrointestinal dysmotility, post-infectious inflammation, altered gut microbiome.
generalGuidance: Low-FODMAP dietary trial, soluble fiber (psyllium), antispasmodics, neuromodulators, gut-directed cognitive behavioral therapy.
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical assessment for "red flag" symptoms: nocturnal symptoms, unintended weight loss, rectal bleeding, or onset after age 50.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by relation to meals, stool characteristics, and localized peritoneal signs.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Chronic Constipation
description: A functional gastrointestinal condition marked by infrequent, difficult, or incomplete evacuation of dry, hardened stool.
causes: Inadequate dietary fiber, insufficient hydration, pelvic floor dyssynergia, slow transit colonic motility, side effect of medications.
generalGuidance: Bulk-forming laxatives (psyllium), osmotic laxatives (polyethylene glycol), pelvic floor physical therapy, biofeedback.
whenToSeekCare: Consult a physician if constipation is accompanied by severe abdominal distension, vomiting, rectal bleeding, or sudden onset in older adults.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by relation to meals, stool characteristics, and localized peritoneal signs.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Chronic Diarrhea
description: Frequent loose, watery stools persisting continuously or intermittently for greater than four weeks in duration.
causes: Inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's/Colitis), celiac disease, malabsorption syndromes, chronic parasitic infection, microscopic colitis.
riskFactors: family history of IBD or celiac disease
generalGuidance: Etiology-specific treatment (gluten-free diet for celiac, anti-inflammatory therapy for IBD), electrolyte replenishment, anti-diarrheal agents.
whenToSeekCare: Seek thorough clinical evaluation for chronic diarrhea accompanied by unintended weight loss, fever, anemia, or visible blood in stool.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by relation to meals, stool characteristics, and localized peritoneal signs.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Gallstones
description: Hardened mineral deposits formed inside the gallbladder, predominantly composed of crystallized cholesterol or bilirubin pigments.
causes: Supersaturation of bile with cholesterol, gallbladder hypomotility, excessive biliary bilirubin secretion.
prevention: Maintain a healthy body weight gradually (avoid crash starvation diets)
eat a balanced fiber-rich diet with healthy unsaturated fats.
generalGuidance: Observation for asymptomatic stones; laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic recurrent biliary colic or acute cholecystitis.
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency medical evaluation for severe right upper quadrant pain radiating to shoulder, fever, persistent vomiting, or jaundice.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by relation to meals, stool characteristics, and localized peritoneal signs.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Tension Headache
description: The most prevalent type of primary headache, presenting as mild-to-moderate dull, band-like tightening pressure across the head and neck.
causes: Myofascial trigger points, pericranial muscle tenderness, central pain sensitization, prolonged emotional stress.
prevention: stretching of cervical and shoulder muscles.
generalGuidance: Over-the-counter analgesics (acetaminophen, NSAIDs), physical therapy, stress management techniques, tricyclic antidepressants for chronic cases.
redFlags: Focal neurological deficits (facial droop, arm weakness)
whenToSeekCare: Seek evaluation for sudden severe "thunderclap" headache, new headaches after age 50, or associated focal neurological deficits.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by neurological exam and temporal symptom onset.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Peripheral Neuropathy
description: Damage to the peripheral nervous system leading to weakness, numbness, tingling, or burning sensations primarily in hands and feet.
causes: Diabetic microvascular axonal damage, chronic alcoholism, vitamin B12 deficiency, chemotherapy toxicity, autoimmune disorders.
prevention: Strict blood glucose control in diabetes
generalGuidance: Optimization of underlying cause, neuropathic pain agents (gabapentin, pregabalin, duloxetine), physical therapy, daily foot inspections.
redFlags: Focal neurological deficits (facial droop, arm weakness)
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical attention for progressive numbness spreading upward, unhealed foot ulcers, or difficulty with balance and walking.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by neurological exam and temporal symptom onset.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Kidney Stones
description: Solid mineral and acid salt crystalline aggregations that form within renal calyces and pass into the urinary tract.
causes: Supersaturation of urine with calcium, oxalate, phosphate, or uric acid coupled with inadequate urinary fluid volume.
prevention: Drink 2.5 to 3 liters of water daily to maintain clear dilute urine
limit sodium and excess animal protein
generalGuidance: Adequate hydration, alpha-blockers (tamsulosin) to aid stone passage, oral analgesia, shock-wave lithotripsy or ureteroscopy for large stones.
redFlags: High fever with severe flank rigors
whenToSeekCare: Seek immediate emergency care for intractable flank pain, persistent vomiting, inability to urinate, or high fever with chills.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by urinalysis and renal function indices.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Kidney Infection (Pyelonephritis)
description: An acute bacterial infection of the renal parenchyma and renal pelvis, usually ascending from the lower urinary tract.
causes: Ascending spread of uropathogenic bacteria (primarily Escherichia coli) from cystitis through ureters into the kidney.
riskFactors: Untreated or recurrent lower urinary tract infections
generalGuidance: Empirical and culture-directed oral or intravenous antibiotics for 7-14 days, antipyretics, adequate oral or IV fluid hydration.
redFlags: High fever with severe flank rigors
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency medical care immediately for high fever, severe flank pain, shaking chills, nausea, or confusion.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by urinalysis and renal function indices.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Acne Vulgaris
description: A chronic inflammatory dermatological disorder of the pilosebaceous units characterized by comedones, papules, pustules, or cysts.
causes: Excess sebum production, follicular hyperkeratinization, Cutibacterium acnes bacterial proliferation, and inflammatory mediator release.
prevention: Gentle non-abrasive facial cleansing twice daily
generalGuidance: Topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, topical/oral antibiotics, salicylic acid, hormonal therapies (oral contraceptives, spironolactone), oral isotretinoin.
redFlags: Rapidly expanding erythema with systemic high fever
whenToSeekCare: Seek dermatological consultation for painful deep cysts, scarring acne lesions, or lack of response to non-prescription remedies.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by lesion morphology, distribution, and epidermal barrier changes.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Eczema (Atopic Dermatitis)
description: A chronic, pruritic inflammatory skin condition characterized by defective epidermal barrier function and immune dysregulation.
causes: Genetic mutations in the filaggrin (FLG) gene, epidermal skin barrier disruption, Th2-skewed immune hyperreactivity.
riskFactors: Personal or family history of atopy (asthma
prevention: Frequent skin moisturization with bland thick emollient ointments
generalGuidance: Liberal emollient moisturizers, topical corticosteroids, topical calcineurin inhibitors, phototherapy, biologic therapies (dupilumab).
redFlags: Rapidly expanding erythema with systemic high fever
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical attention if eczema lesions exhibit signs of bacterial superinfection (honey-colored crusting, pustules, severe pain).
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by lesion morphology, distribution, and epidermal barrier changes.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Psoriasis
description: A chronic autoimmune inflammatory dermatosis characterized by well-demarcated erythematous plaques covered with silvery micaceous scales.
causes: Immune-mediated acceleration of epidermal keratinocyte turnover driven by the IL-23/IL-17 cytokine signaling pathway.
generalGuidance: Topical corticosteroids, topical vitamin D analogs, phototherapy (narrowband UVB), systemic methotrexate, biologic targeted agents.
redFlags: Rapidly expanding erythema with systemic high fever
whenToSeekCare: Consult a dermatologist for extensive cutaneous involvement, severe discomfort, or associated joint pain (psoriatic arthritis).
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by lesion morphology, distribution, and epidermal barrier changes.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Contact Dermatitis
description: An acute or chronic cutaneous inflammatory reaction elicited by direct contact with an external chemical, allergen, or physical irritant.
causes: Either direct cytotoxic irritant injury (Irritant Contact Dermatitis) or delayed Type IV cell-mediated allergy (Allergic Contact Dermatitis).
prevention: Identify and rigorously avoid contact with causative allergens or irritants
wash skin immediately after accidental exposure.
generalGuidance: Cool wet compresses, topical corticosteroid creams, oral antihistamines for pruritus, barrier repair creams.
redFlags: Rapidly expanding erythema with systemic high fever
whenToSeekCare: Seek care if dermatitis affects eyes, face, or genitalia, spreads rapidly, or develops secondary bacterial pustules or cellulitis.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by lesion morphology, distribution, and epidermal barrier changes.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Fungal Skin Infection
description: Superficial fungal colonization of the keratinized layer of skin, hair, or nails caused by dermatophytes or yeasts.
causes: Dermatophyte fungi (Trichophyton, Microsporum, Epidermophyton) or Candida albicans yeast proliferating in warm, humid skin folds.
prevention: wear sandals in public locker rooms and showers.
generalGuidance: Topical antifungal creams (clotrimazole, terbinafine, miconazole) applied for 2-4 weeks, oral antifungals for widespread or nail infections.
redFlags: Rapidly expanding erythema with systemic high fever
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical consultation if fungal rash does not improve after 2 weeks of over-the-counter treatment or spreads extensively.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by lesion morphology, distribution, and epidermal barrier changes.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Urticaria (Hives)
description: A transient vascular reaction of the dermis characterized by intensely pruritic, raised, erythematous wheals with surrounding flare.
causes: Mast cell and basophil degranulation with rapid release of histamine and vasodilatory mediators triggered by allergens, infections, or physical stimuli.
prevention: Identify and avoid known specific triggering allergens
avoid unneeded NSAIDs during acute flares.
generalGuidance: Second-generation H1-antihistamines (cetirizine, fexofenadine, loratadine), H2-blockers, cool compresses, oral corticosteroids for severe flares.
redFlags: Rapidly expanding erythema with systemic high fever
whenToSeekCare: Seek immediate emergency care if hives occur with facial/lip/tongue swelling (angioedema), difficulty breathing, or dizziness (anaphylaxis).
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by lesion morphology, distribution, and epidermal barrier changes.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Osteoarthritis
description: A progressive degenerative joint disease characterized by breakdown of articular cartilage, subchondral bone remodeling, and osteophyte formation.
causes: Biomechanical joint stress, age-related chondrocyte senescence, repetitive mechanical microtrauma, low-grade joint inflammation.
prevention: Maintain healthy body weight to reduce knee/hip mechanical loading
generalGuidance: Physical therapy, quadriceps muscle strengthening, weight loss, acetaminophen or topical NSAIDs, intra-articular injections, joint replacement surgery.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Consult an orthopedic specialist for progressive joint pain limiting ambulation or daily self-care activities.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
description: A chronic, systemic autoimmune disease characterized by symmetric inflammatory polyarthritis, synovial proliferation, and progressive joint destruction.
causes: Autoimmune targeting of synovial tissue by autoantibodies (Rheumatoid Factor, anti-CCP), leading to chronic pannus formation and cartilage erosion.
prevention: early diagnostic assessment upon onset of symmetric joint swelling.
generalGuidance: Disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs, e.g. methotrexate), biologic TNF/IL-6 inhibitors, short-term corticosteroids, physical therapy.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent rheumatology evaluation within weeks of developing persistent symmetric joint swelling, morning stiffness > 1 hour, or hand deformities.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Osteoporosis
description: A systemic skeletal disease characterized by low bone mineral density and microarchitectural deterioration, resulting in heightened bone fragility.
causes: Imbalance between osteoclastic bone resorption and osteoblastic bone formation, accelerated by postmenopausal estrogen decline or aging.
prevention: Adequate dietary calcium and vitamin D
regular weight-bearing and resistance training exercises
generalGuidance: Antiresorptive medications (bisphosphonates, denosumab), anabolic agents (teriparatide), calcium and vitamin D supplementation, DEXA scans.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical care following any low-trauma fall resulting in severe bone/hip pain, or progressive height loss and dorsal kyphosis.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Gout
description: A painful form of inflammatory crystal arthritis caused by the deposition of monosodium urate monohydrate crystals within articular and periarticular tissues.
causes: Persistent hyperuricemia exceeding the saturation threshold due to renal urate underexcretion or excessive purine metabolism.
generalGuidance: Acute flare: NSAIDs, colchicine, or corticosteroids. Long-term management: urate-lowering therapy (allopurinol, febuxostat) targeting uric acid < 6 mg/dL.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt care for acute, excruciating monoarticular joint swelling (commonly the first metatarsophalangeal big toe joint).
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Muscle Strain
description: An acute or repetitive stretch injury causing tearing of muscle fibers or their associated myotendinous junctions.
causes: Overstretching, excessive eccentric muscular load, sudden violent contraction, or repetitive ergonomic fatigue without adequate warm-up.
prevention: Thorough dynamic warm-up before athletic activity
generalGuidance: R.I.C.E. protocol (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation) initially, brief course of oral NSAIDs, gentle progressive stretching, physical therapy.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for an audible muscle "pop", severe inability to bear weight, visible muscular defect, or significant hematoma.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Vitamin B12 Deficiency
description: A nutritional hematological and neurological disorder caused by insufficient cobalamin levels, leading to megaloblastic anemia and neuropathy.
causes: Pernicious anemia (autoimmune destruction of gastric parietal cells / lack of intrinsic factor), strict vegan diet without supplementation, malabsorption.
riskFactors: chronic proton pump inhibitor or metformin use
prior gastric bypass or ileal resection
prevention: fortified cereals) or take regular oral cobalamin supplements if adhering to plant-based diets.
generalGuidance: Oral high-dose vitamin B12 (1000 mcg daily) or intramuscular cyanocobalamin/hydroxocobalamin injections until stores are replenished.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for persistent numbness in extremities, unsteady gait, cognitive changes, or unexplained fatigue and pale skin.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Vitamin D Deficiency
description: A systemic nutritional insufficiency resulting from inadequate synthesis or dietary intake of calciferol, impairing calcium and bone homeostasis.
causes: Limited cutaneous synthesis from sunlight exposure, low dietary intake, malabsorption, renal/hepatic conversion impairments, pigmented skin.
prevention: consuming vitamin D-fortified milk/cereals and fatty fish
generalGuidance: High-dose oral ergocalciferol (D2) or cholecalciferol (D3) therapy, followed by long-term maintenance supplementation and serum 25(OH)D monitoring.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Seek healthcare consultation for persistent diffuse musculoskeletal aching, proximal muscle weakness, or recurrent bone stress fractures.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Sickle Cell Disease
description: An inherited genetic hemoglobinopathy caused by a point mutation in the beta-globin gene, resulting in abnormal sickle-shaped red blood cells.
causes: Homozygous inheritance of the HbS allele (glutamic acid substituted by valine at position 6 of the beta-globin chain).
riskFactors: or South Asian ancestral descent; positive parental sickle cell carrier status.
generalGuidance: Hydroxyurea to boost fetal hemoglobin, routine vaccinations, prophylactic penicillin in children, hydration, multimodal pain crisis protocols.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Seek immediate emergency medical care for acute vaso-occlusive pain crises, acute chest syndrome (chest pain/fever/cough), or stroke symptoms.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Generalized Anxiety
description: An educational screening category for persistent, excessive, and uncontrollable worry regarding various everyday life events and activities.
causes: Dysregulation of amygdala-prefrontal neurocircuitry, neurotransmitter imbalances (GABA, serotonin, norepinephrine), chronic psychosocial stress.
generalGuidance: Evidence-based cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), mindfulness-based stress reduction, SSRI or SNRI medications under psychiatric guidance.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent mental health evaluation if anxiety causes panic attacks, severe functional impairment, or suicidal thoughts.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Depressive Symptoms
description: An educational screening category for persistent depressed mood, loss of interest or pleasure, low energy, and feelings of worthlessness.
causes: Interactions between genetic vulnerability, neurochemical alterations, neuroendocrine dysregulation (HPA axis), and adverse life events.
generalGuidance: Psychotherapy (CBT, interpersonal therapy), structured exercise programs, antidepressant pharmacotherapy (SSRIs) supervised by clinicians.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Seek immediate emergency support or call a crisis lifeline (988 in the US) if experiencing thoughts of self-harm or suicide.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Chronic Stress & Burnout
description: A state of chronic physical and psychological exhaustion coupled with emotional depletion caused by prolonged unmanaged stress.
causes: Sustained activation of the sympathetic-adreno-medullary and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axes without adequate recovery phases.
generalGuidance: Workplace/lifestyle restructuring, stress reduction coaching, sleep optimization, mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR), clinical counseling.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Seek professional psychological consultation if burnout leads to chronic depressive feelings, severe insomnia, or panic attacks.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Insomnia & Sleep Disorder
description: A condition characterized by persistent difficulty initiating, consolidating, or maintaining restorative sleep despite adequate opportunity.
causes: Hyperarousal states of the central nervous system, circadian rhythm misalignment, poor sleep ergonomics, psychological distress.
riskFactors: blue light screen use in bed
prevention: Strict sleep hygiene: consistent sleep-wake schedule
generalGuidance: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) as first-line gold standard, stimulus control, sleep restriction therapy, short-term sleep aids.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Consult a sleep specialist or physician if sleep disruption persists over 3 months, causes daytime sleepiness, or is accompanied by loud snoring/gasping.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Metabolic Syndrome
description: A clustering of at least three concurrent cardiometabolic risk factors including central obesity, hypertension, hypertriglyceridemia, low HDL, and impaired fasting glucose.
causes: Visceral adiposity-induced chronic low-grade inflammation, adipokine dysregulation, and systemic peripheral insulin resistance.
prevention: 150 minutes/week moderate aerobic exercise plus resistance training
maintaining waist circumference < 40 in (men) or < 35 in (women).
generalGuidance: Intensive therapeutic lifestyle intervention, targeted pharmacological management of individual risk factors (statins, antihypertensives, metformin).
redFlags: Severe lethargy with fruity acetone breath odor
whenToSeekCare: Consult your primary healthcare provider for comprehensive cardiometabolic blood panel screening and personalized prevention planning.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by glycemic and hormonal biomarker laboratory panels.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Fever
description: A temporary elevation in body temperature above normal (typically > 38°C or 100.4°F), often serving as an adaptive physiological defense against infection.
causes: Viral infections (influenza, common cold, COVID-19), bacterial pathogens (strep, urinary infections), inflammatory conditions, or immunization responses.
riskFactors: extreme physical exertion in hot environments.
prevention: avoiding close contact with sick persons
generalGuidance: Adequate fluid replenishment, rest, antipyretics (acetaminophen or ibuprofen if clinically suitable), light clothing, and room temperature control.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care for temperature > 39.4°C (103°F), fever lasting > 3 days, stiff neck, confusion, breathing difficulty, or persistent vomiting.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Dehydration
description: A deficit in total body water resulting from fluid loss exceeding intake, disrupting vital cellular and metabolic electrolyte homeostasis.
causes: Inadequate fluid intake, profuse perspiration from heat or exertion, prolonged vomiting, diarrhea, high fever, or untreated diabetes mellitus.
prevention: Drink clean fluids regularly throughout the day
increase intake during exercise or hot weather
generalGuidance: Oral rehydration therapy with balanced oral electrolyte solutions; severe cases require intravenous isotonic crystalloid hydration.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency medical evaluation for severe dizziness, confusion, inability to keep liquids down, absence of urination > 8 hours, or fainting.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Fatigue
description: A persistent, overwhelming feeling of physical or mental exhaustion that is not relieved by normal sleep and impairs daily functional capacity.
causes: Chronic sleep deficiency, anemia, hypothyroidism, major depression, fibromyalgia, chronic infections, poor nutrition, or underlying systemic disease.
prevention: engage in daily moderate physical exercise
generalGuidance: Investigate and address underlying systemic causes, cognitive behavioral sleep therapy, balanced nutrition, graded physical exercise.
redFlags: Severe disorientation or altered mental status
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical evaluation if fatigue is accompanied by unexplained weight loss, shortness of breath, chest pain, or swollen lymph nodes.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by clinical progression and systemic examination.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Coronary Artery Disease
description: Impairment of blood flow through coronary arteries caused by progressive atherosclerotic plaque buildup, restricting myocardial oxygenation.
causes: Atherosclerosis initiated by endothelial injury, lipid accumulation, and chronic vascular inflammation.
riskFactors: family history of early heart disease.
prevention: maintain healthy blood pressure and lipid levels
generalGuidance: Statins, antiplatelet therapy (aspirin), beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, cardiac rehabilitation, and percutaneous coronary intervention when indicated.
redFlags: Crushing chest pressure radiating to arm or jaw
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care immediately for crushing chest pain, pain radiating to jaw or left arm, cold sweats, or sudden shortness of breath.
differentiatingFeatures: Characterized by exertional triggers and cardiac biomarker changes.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Stroke
description: Acute neurological deficit caused by disrupted cerebral perfusion (ischemic stroke, 87%) or intracranial vascular rupture (hemorrhagic stroke).
causes: Thromboembolism from large-artery atherosclerosis, cardiac emboli (atrial fibrillation), or cerebral aneurysm/arteriovenous malformation rupture.
generalGuidance: Immediate emergency thrombolysis (IV rtPA) within 4.5 hours, mechanical endovascular thrombectomy, neurointensive monitoring, rehabilitation.
redFlags: Focal neurological deficits (facial droop, arm weakness)
whenToSeekCare: CALL EMERGENCY IMMEDIATELY upon any FAST sign: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call emergency.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by neurological exam and temporal symptom onset.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Melanoma
description: The most aggressive form of skin cancer arising from malignant transformation of melanocytes, capable of rapid metastatic dissemination if untreated.
causes: DNA damage primarily induced by solar ultraviolet (UV) radiation (especially intermittent sunburns) and genetic mutations (BRAF, CDKN2A).
prevention: seeking shade during peak UV hours (10 AM - 4 PM)
generalGuidance: Wide local surgical excision, sentinel lymph node biopsy, targeted molecular therapies (BRAF/MEK inhibitors), immune checkpoint inhibitors (PD-1).
redFlags: Rapidly expanding erythema with systemic high fever
whenToSeekCare: Consult a dermatologist promptly for any mole exhibiting ABCDE warning signs (Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variegation, Diameter >6mm, Evolving).
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by lesion morphology, distribution, and epidermal barrier changes.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Basal Cell Carcinoma
description: The most prevalent cutaneous malignancy worldwide, arising from basal keratinocytes, characterized by slow growth and rare distant metastasis.
causes: Cumulative chronic ultraviolet (UVB/UVA) radiation exposure damaging PTCH1 and p53 tumor suppressor genes.
prevention: wearing wide-brimmed hats and UV-blocking sunglasses
generalGuidance: Surgical excision, Mohs micrographic surgery for facial lesions, curettage and electrodesiccation, topical imiquimod, or targeted Hedgehog inhibitors.
redFlags: Rapidly expanding erythema with systemic high fever
whenToSeekCare: Seek dermatological evaluation for pearly pink bumps with rolled edges, non-healing sores that bleed easily, or persistent scaly patches.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by lesion morphology, distribution, and epidermal barrier changes.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review

name: Actinic Keratosis
description: A pre-malignant cutaneous lesion caused by chronic ultraviolet damage, presenting as rough, scaly or gritty patches that may progress to squamous cell carcinoma.
causes: Cumulative lifetime ultraviolet radiation inducing TP53 mutations in epidermal keratinocytes.
prevention: wearing UV protective hats and clothing
generalGuidance: Cryotherapy with liquid nitrogen, topical 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), imiquimod cream, photodynamic therapy (PDT), field directed therapies.
redFlags: Rapidly expanding erythema with systemic high fever
whenToSeekCare: Consult a dermatologist for rough, sandpaper-like or crusty skin spots that persist, enlarge, become tender, or develop indurated bases.
differentiatingFeatures: Differentiated by lesion morphology, distribution, and epidermal barrier changes.
source: CDC Clinical Practice Guidelines / WHO Disease Reference / Mayo Clinic Clinical Review
